newsitem.title: USA: Times Mirror second quarter shows newspaper strength.
newsitem.headline: Times Mirror second quarter shows newspaper strength.

text.p: Times Mirror Co. Thursday reported higher second-quarter earnings, aided by strength in its core newspaper business and higher advertising revenues.

Times Mirror publishes the Los Angeles Times, Newsday, The Baltimore Sun and other newspapers; professional information for the legal, health sciences, aviation, and training markets and consumer magazines.

"Second-quarter results reflect continued strength in the newspaper publishing segment with all our newspapers reporting solid increases in advertising revenues and lower newsprint pricing," said Mark H. Willes, Times Mirror chairman.

However, the company expects the rate of earnings growth to slow somewhat in the second half of 1997 because of anticipated increases in newsprint prices and consolidation expenses in the Professional Information segment.
Los Angeles-based Times Mirror had second-quarter earnings of $66 million, or 58 cents per share, compared with $46.0 million, or 33 cents per share, a year earlier.
Revenues for the 1997 quarter declined to $811.8 million from $837.3 million in the prior year due to divestitures in the Professional Information business.

For the first half of 1997, the company reported earnings of $111.2 million, or 94 cents per share, up from $72.1 million, or 47 cents per share, in the prior year's first half. First-half 1997 revenues were $1.59 billion, compared with $1.64 billion in the prior year.

Times Mirror's newspaper operating profit rose 48.0 percent to $112.4 million, due to revenue gains as well as a substantial year-over-year decline in newsprint expenses. For the quarter, newsprint expenses declined almost 17 percent from the prior year as higher consumption due to continued circulation growth was more than offset by lower newsprint prices.
Newspaper Publishing total revenues rose 6 percent, with advertising revenues up 7.3 percent to $419.9 million from $391.3 million in the prior-year quarter.
Comparisons in the Professional Information segment were affected by the sale of college and scientific publishing operations and the completion of a joint venture.

The segment's second-quarter 1997 revenues were $197.2 million, compared with $256.9 million in the prior year. The segment's 1997 second-quarter operating profit declined to $24.4 million from $27.2 million in the prior year, reflecting additional expenses incurred with the continuing consolidation at the Mosby-Year Book division.
The magazine publishing segment had an operating profit of $5.3 million, compared with a small loss in the prior year, aided by higher advertising revenues.
Times Mirror also said it bought back about 2.5 million shares of its Series A common stock in April and early May at a total cost of $129.8 million.
Times Mirror's stock was down $2.125 at $55.0625 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
